hint.en: Start from what happened, not from what you concluded about yourself.
hint.zh: 从「发生了什么」开始，不从「我是个什么人」开始。

hint.en: Look across your own records instead of answering in the moment.
hint.zh: 把眼光放到你自己记下的那些条上，而不是只回答此刻。

hint.en: One action small enough to try, and what you would count as its result.
hint.zh: 一个小到能试的行动，以及你打算凭什么说它有结果。

hint.en: An insight earns trust by pointing back at your own records.
hint.zh: 洞察要靠指回你自己的记录来赢得信任。

title.en: What the camera would have caught

question.en: Write one thing that happened today using only what a camera and a microphone could have caught — no adjectives about people.
question.zh: 写下今天发生的一件事，只写摄像机和麦克风拍得到的部分——不写对人的形容。

why.en: Once the event and your reading of it sit in different sentences, you have something you can check later.
why.zh: 事件和你的解读分在两句里，之后才有可对的东西。

follow_up.en: Which words in your sentence would the camera have missed?
follow_up.zh: 你那句话里，哪些词是摄像机拍不到的？

title.zh: 给一种感觉起朴素的名字

question.en: Name today's main feeling in the dullest words you can find, then write the moment it started.
question.zh: 用你能找到的最平淡的词说出今天主要的那个感觉，再写下它开始的那一刻。

why.en: Grand words finish the story too early; a plain name leaves the moment describable.
why.zh: 大词会把故事提前写完，朴素的名称才让那个时刻还能被描述。

follow_up.en: Would you still use that word if a stranger read the sentence?
follow_up.zh: 如果换个陌生人读这句，你还会用同一个词吗？

title.en: What the feeling made you do
title.zh: 那个感觉让你做了什么

question.en: Pick one action from today and write what it cost you and what it saved you.
question.zh: 挑今天的一个动作，写下它花了你什么、又给你省了什么。

why.en: Behaviour is easier to verify than mood, and the cost is where the trade-off shows.
why.zh: 行为比情绪好核对，而取舍就写在代价里。

follow_up.en: Would you pay that cost again tomorrow?
follow_up.zh: 明天你还愿意付一次这个代价吗？

question.en: Write the smallest thing you meant to do today and did not, without explaining why.
question.zh: 写下今天你本来要做、最小额度上没做的一件事，先不解释原因。

why.en: Explanation arrives fast and hides the fact; the unexplained gap is the useful part.
why.zh: 原因来得太快会把事实盖住，那个没解释的空档才是有用的部分。

follow_up.en: What is the first sentence you would write if it got done?
follow_up.zh: 如果它被做完了，你会写下的第一句是什么？

question.en: Find one moment today that turned out less bad than you had predicted, and write what you had expected.
question.zh: 找今天一个比你预想的要好的时刻，并写下你原本预计会怎样。

why.en: Predictions you never write down can't be corrected; this one can.
why.zh: 没写下来的预计没法修正，这一条可以。

follow_up.en: How did you know it would be that bad — what was the evidence?
follow_up.zh: 你凭什么判定会那么糟——依据是什么？

question.en: Choose one conversation from today and write what you were paying attention to while it happened.
question.zh: 挑今天的一段对话，写下当时你的注意力真正落在什么上面。

why.en: What you listened for shapes what you remember, and the record keeps only one version.
why.zh: 你在听什么决定了你记住什么，而记录只留一个版本。

follow_up.en: What did the other person probably want you to notice?
follow_up.zh: 对方大概希望你注意到的是什么？

title.en: The need you didn't say out loud
title.zh: 你没说出口的那个需要

question.en: Write one thing you wanted today and asked for differently — or not at all.
question.zh: 写下今天你其实想要、但用了别的方式绕（或压根没提）的一件事。

why.en: Indirect requests are the clearest evidence of what you expect to happen when you ask.
why.zh: 绕弯的请求最能说明：你预计开口之后会发生什么。

follow_up.en: What did you think would happen if you had said it directly?
follow_up.zh: 如果你当时直接说，你猜会发生什么？

question.en: Write where you felt today's tension physically, and what had happened in the ten minutes before.
question.zh: 写下今天那份紧绷在身体哪里，以及之前十分钟发生了什么。

why.en: A physical marker plus a preceding event gives you two things to compare next time.
why.zh: 一个身体标记加上前因事件，下次就有两样东西可比。

follow_up.en: Has this pairing shown up in your earlier check-ins?
follow_up.zh: 这个搭配在你以前的签到里出现过吗？

question.en: Look back through your records and copy out a sentence you have basically written more than once.
question.zh: 翻你自己的记录，抄出一句你基本上写过不止一次的话。

why.en: Repetition is the only long-term signal this app can honestly show you; the wording is the data.
why.zh: 重复是这个应用能诚实给你的长期信号，措辞本身就是数据。

follow_up.en: In the version you wrote first, what did you want that you don't mention now?
follow_up.zh: 在你最早写的那版里，有什么是现在没提的？

title.zh: 同样的处境，不同的反应

question.en: Find two entries about a similar situation and write how your reaction differed between them.
question.zh: 找两条关于相似处境的记录，写下你两次反应哪里不一样。

why.en: Difference inside the same kind of event is the evidence that something moved.
why.zh: 同类事件内部的差别，才是「有东西变了」的证据。

follow_up.en: What was different around you, not inside you?
follow_up.zh: 你周围的什么变了，而不是你里面的什么变了？

question.en: Write a claim about yourself that your own records contradict, and name the record that contradicts it.
question.zh: 写一句关于你自己的说法，它被你自己的记录反驳了——指出是哪条记录。

why.en: A belief loses force when it has a dated counter-example attached to it.
why.zh: 一个信念挂上带日期的反例之后，就没那么有权威了。

follow_up.en: Why does that one entry not count, in your view?
follow_up.zh: 按你的看法，那条记录为什么不算数？

question.en: Write your most recent "I'll be fine once..." sentence, then list what actually has to happen for it.
question.zh: 写下你最近一句「等我……就好了」，再列出它真的需要发生什么。

why.en: Conditions deferred forever are the place where your effort keeps going instead of into an action.
why.zh: 永远往后推的前提，是你把力气花在等待而不是行动上的地方。

follow_up.en: Which part of that condition is inside one of your actions?
follow_up.zh: 那个前提里，哪一部分落在你能做的动作内？

question.en: List three things you did in the last month that nobody was told about.
question.zh: 列出最近一个月你做过的、没告诉任何人的三件事。

why.en: Unannounced actions are the least decorated evidence of what you actually do when it counts.
why.zh: 没宣告的行动是最不加修饰的证据，说明要紧的时候你真的会做什么。

follow_up.en: What do those three have in common that you would not say out loud?
follow_up.zh: 这三件有什么共同点是你不会说出口的？

question.en: Open an entry from at least three months ago and quote one sentence you would not write today.
question.zh: 打开一条至少三个月前的记录，引一句你今天不会那样写的话。

why.en: Change you can quote is more solid than change you feel; the quote stays checkable.
why.zh: 能引出来的变化比感觉到的变化结实，因为引文还能被查。

follow_up.en: What did that version of you get right that you still haven't acted on?
follow_up.zh: 那时你看对了什么、而现在还没去做？

title.en: The good weeks looked like something

question.en: Pick your two best weeks in the records and write what was in them that this week lacks.
question.zh: 从记录里挑你最好的两周，写下里面有而本周没有的东西。

why.en: Concrete conditions from your own history are worth more than generic advice about routine.
why.zh: 来自你自己历史的具体条件，比通用的作息建议值钱。

follow_up.en: Which of those was ever actually under your control?
follow_up.zh: 其中哪些是你真的能控制的？

title.en: The pattern you'd rather not name
title.zh: 你不太想命名的那个规律

question.en: Describe, in neutral words, something that keeps recurring in your entries and that you never comment on.
question.zh: 用中性的词描述一件在你记录里反复出现、但你从不评论的事。

why.en: What a record consistently omits is as informative as what it repeats.
why.zh: 记录里始终被略掉的东西，和被反复写下的东西一样有信息量。

follow_up.en: What would change if you wrote it down once, factually?
follow_up.zh: 如果你按事实写下一次，什么会改变？

question.en: Choose one action you can finish before tomorrow morning and write how you'll know it happened.
question.zh: 选一个明早之前能做完的动作，写下你凭什么知道它做了。

why.en: An action with a checkable trace becomes a record; without one it stays a wish.
why.zh: 有可查痕迹的行动会变成记录，没有就还是愿望。

follow_up.en: What is the smallest version of that action that still counts?
follow_up.zh: 它最小、但仍算数的版本是什么？

title.en: What you planned here and actually did
title.zh: 在这里计划过、真做了的

question.en: Pick one action you wrote here earlier and report what happened, in one or two sentences, without grading yourself.
question.zh: 挑一条你之前在这里写下的行动，用一两句话汇报结果，先不给自己打分。

why.en: Closing the loop on your own predictions is how this app gets a result instead of a to-do list.
why.zh: 把自己写过的预测闭环，是这个应用拿到「结果」而不是「待办清单」的方式。

follow_up.en: Was the gap in the action, the plan, or the estimate of difficulty?
follow_up.zh: 差距在动作上、计划上，还是难度的估计上？

title.en: If it goes well, what differs
title.zh: 如果顺利，哪里会不一样

question.en: Before acting, write one observable difference that will exist if this goes well.
question.zh: 行动之前，先写下一个「顺利的话会出现」的、可观察的差别。

why.en: A difference you can observe is also a difference you can be wrong about, which is the useful kind.
why.zh: 能观察的差别也意味着可能出错，而这一种才有用。

follow_up.en: Who else would notice that difference?
follow_up.zh: 还有谁会注意到这个差别？

question.en: Write the two assumptions your next step depends on, and mark which one you have evidence for.
question.zh: 写下你下一步依赖的两个假设，标出哪一个你是有依据的。

why.en: Most stalled steps are waiting on an assumption nobody checked.
why.zh: 大多数卡住的步骤，是在等一个没人检查过的假设。

follow_up.en: What is the cheapest way to test the unchecked one?
follow_up.zh: 测那个没依据的假设，最便宜的办法是什么？

question.en: Write what your last commitment actually cost — time, money, sleep, or something you gave up.
question.zh: 写下你上一个承诺实际的花费——时间、钱、睡眠，还是你放弃的什么。

why.en: Costs you never write down make every future plan look free.
why.zh: 没记下的代价会让以后每个计划都看起来很便宜。

follow_up.en: Would you budget that cost again, knowing the number?
follow_up.zh: 知道这个数字以后，你还会这样预算吗？

question.en: Describe the moment you quit something that was still working, and what came just before it.
question.zh: 描述一次你在事情还有进展时就停下的时刻，以及它前面发生了什么。

why.en: Early stops usually have a trigger, and a trigger is something you can see coming next time.
why.zh: 提前停下通常有个诱因，而诱因是下次能提前看见的东西。

follow_up.en: What would you have needed, in that exact moment, to continue one more step?
follow_up.zh: 在那一刻，你需要什么才能再多走一步？

question.en: Write a date, and the one thing you will look for on that date to decide whether this mattered.
question.zh: 写一个日期，以及那天你会看的唯一一件事，用它来判断这件事是否重要。

why.en: Judgement needs a date attached; otherwise the same question gets re-asked every week without new evidence.
why.zh: 判断需要挂一个日期，否则同一个问题每周被重问一次、依据却没变。

follow_up.en: What result would make you call this closed and move on?
follow_up.zh: 什么样的结果会让你说「这事结了」然后往前走？

title.en: Which record is that claim from?

question.en: Take one AI insight you were shown, and write which of your entries it could have come from. If none, say none.
question.zh: 挑一条你看到的 AI 洞察，写下它可能来自你的哪条记录；没有就写「没有」。

why.en: An insight with no source in your own records is decoration, however accurate it sounds.
why.zh: 在你的记录里找不到出处的洞察，无论听着多准，都只是装饰。

follow_up.en: Does the insight survive if you remove that entry?
follow_up.zh: 把那条记录去掉，这条洞察还站得住吗？

question.en: For a pattern you were told about, write one entry where it did not hold.
question.zh: 对一条告诉你的规律，写出一条它不成立的记录。

why.en: Patterns that survive your own counter-examples are worth acting on; the rest are summaries.
why.zh: 能扛住你自己反例的规律值得行动，其余的只是摘要。

follow_up.en: Does the counter-example weaken the pattern or narrow it?
follow_up.zh: 这个反例是削弱了规律，还是缩小了它的范围？

question.en: Rewrite one insight as if a stranger who had never seen your records wrote it, and note what changes.
question.zh: 把一条洞察改写成「一个从没看过你记录的陌生人」写出来的样子，记下什么变了。

why.en: Generic wording is the tell that the insight wasn't really about you.
why.zh: 套话式的措辞是一个信号：那条洞察其实不是在说你。

follow_up.en: Which half of the rewritten version is still true?
follow_up.zh: 改写后的版本里，哪一半仍然是真的？

title.en: What would make you reject it

question.en: Write what evidence would make you discard this insight, before deciding whether to keep it.
question.zh: 在决定留下这条洞察之前，先写下什么证据会让你丢掉它。

why.en: Deciding the rejection criteria first keeps agreement from being just flattery.
why.zh: 先写拒绝条件，能让你的「同意」不只是被说中了而已。

follow_up.en: If nothing would make you reject it, what is this sentence actually doing for you?
follow_up.zh: 如果没什么能让你拒绝它，那这句话在替你干什么？

question.en: Answer one insight with "agree", "disagree", or "partly" and write the sentence that earns your answer.
question.zh: 对一条洞察回答「同意／不同意／一半」，并写下支撑你这个回答的那句话。

why.en: The record of your disagreement is what makes the matching insights mean something later.
why.zh: 你不同意的那部分被记下来，以后那些说中了的洞察才有分量。

follow_up.en: Which word — agree, disagree, partly — leads to a next action here?
follow_up.zh: 同意、不同意、一半——哪个答案在这里能接出一个行动？

question.en: Find one insight you believe and that you have never acted on; write why acting on it would be hard.
question.zh: 找一条你相信、却从没照着做过的洞察，写下照着做难在哪。

why.en: Agreement is cheap. The obstacle after agreement is where your actual constraint lives.
why.zh: 点头很便宜。点头之后的那个障碍，才是你真实约束在的地方。

follow_up.en: What is the smallest action that would test it despite the obstacle?
follow_up.zh: 绕过那个障碍，能试的最小行动是什么？

title.en: Turn the label back into an event

question.en: Take one word you were described with (avoidant, sensitive, driven...) and write the specific event that earned it.
question.zh: 挑一个用来描述你的词（回避、敏感、有干劲……），写下它具体是从哪件事来的。

why.en: A label without an event can't be argued with, updated, or deleted — and it shouldn't be trusted.
why.zh: 没有事件的标签没法争、没法更新、也没法删——它也不值得被相信。

follow_up.en: If that event had gone differently, would the label still apply?
follow_up.zh: 如果那件事换个走向，这个标签还成立吗？
